source: CPU seconds (user plus system), tests and assertions of each test file as [seconds, tests, assertions], by run: the suite, then the leg as scripts/test-tasks.mjs legOf names it from the environment. A file's seconds are read inside the process that runs it: its import, then its tests from the end of the previous file's last test to the end of its own (test/_run.js), so a process's start-up is no file's, and a split run's files are timed in the processes it splits them over. They are the test process's own: a process a test starts (the CLI, a build, a C compiler) is not counted, which is little of core (its files sum to 11,698 s of the 11,888 CPU s its default run took in all) and most of integration (439 s of 1,353). A file's tests count its skips and todos, as a summary's total does. `measured` says when (the UTC date), at which commit, on what machine, in how many processes, at what load and with how many failing tests each run was taken. test/index.js reads only the ratios within a row: it weighs the processes of a split core or generated run by the seconds of the leg it runs, and a file the row does not list by its bytes at the seconds a byte of those it does (test/_jobs.js estimated). Written only by `node test/index.js --suite=<suite> --costs` under the leg's environment, a run's whole row once every file is timed; an ordinary run never writes it. The hosted suite's seconds are another measure (wall seconds, a file to a process, on the kernel) and stay in test/hosted-costs.json.
